projectList.title: Paralog
projectList.description: A system for emergency medical stations: all the logistics in one place, from the ambulance to headquarters. It replaces spreadsheets, paper and scattered programs, and runs in pilot deployments.
projectList.longDescription:
What Paralog does:
• Mobile app (PWA) for ambulance crews that works offline, with voice entries
• Inventory with stock levels and expiry dates; consumption cards flow automatically from crews to management
• Procurement with automatic vendor assignment
• Invoices with OCR and KSeF integration, public procurement (PZP) contract reconciliation and cost allocation
• Crew scheduling, equipment tracking with service history, and a full audit trail (who, what, when, why)

I build it with AI agents (Claude Code, Codex) and MCP servers.

projectList.title: Bachelor's thesis: abstract reasoning in LLMs (ARC-AGI-2)
projectList.description: An analysis of the capabilities and limitations of the ARC-AGI-2 benchmark as a tool for evaluating reasoning in systems based on large language models. University of Warsaw, 2026.
projectList.longDescription:
Main threads of the thesis:
• Which cognitive abilities ARC-AGI-2 requires: fluid vs crystallized intelligence, relational reasoning, compositionality, working memory
• What has changed in LLM systems: test-time compute, verification loops, self-correction, agentic scaffolding
• What it would actually mean to "solve" ARC-AGI-2 when efficiency and compute cost are part of the evaluation
• The shift from static puzzles to interactive agent benchmarks (ARC-AGI-3)

Conclusion: ARC-AGI-2 is a valuable but limited benchmark. It does not measure general intelligence, but it is an important test of abstract problem solving.

computePower.title: Compute Power
computePower.description: Exponential growth of available compute for AI
computePower.longDescription: The chart shows computing power per dollar (adjusted for inflation). On a logarithmic scale, it shows a smooth line — constant exponential growth since the first programmable computer in 1939, despite wars and crises. When one type of hardware stops being used, the growth rate remains unchanged. The trend spans relays, vacuum tubes, transistors, and integrated circuits — it doesn't rely on any specific paradigm like Moore's Law.
computePower.articleLink: Read more: Why Most of Us Fail to Grasp Coming Exponential Gains in AI

howToUnderstand.title: How to interpret this?
howToUnderstand.content: These indicators illustrate trends in AI development, but are not 'absolute truth'. High benchmark scores ≠ AGI — they show progress but don't guarantee general intelligence. Date predictions come from leading AI researchers and industry leaders, based on trend extrapolation and current capabilities. Remember: these are scenarios, not certainties.
